doc.title: Frank Foster — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Cincinnati bands, race and the road to college
title: Competing interests: photography and girls
summary: Besides music, Foster mentions amateur photography, later developed with Basie, and girls.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Were there any competing interests for you besides music? You seem like you’ve latched on to this fairly early, had all these experiences. What else was competing for space in your head?

The only other thing that could possibly have offered any iota of competition was photography. I became interested in photography, but only as a very amateurish amateur, a beginner. I didn’t develop it until later on with the Basie band. Then I got into 35 millimeter cameras and all that kind of thing.
We’re now going back to Wilberforce and you were sorting out -­
There were girls too. Yeah, I forgot that.
We ain’t really interested in that stuff. You told us how you got deflowered. That’s enough.
Until we get to talk about the love of your life. That’s another story.
